title: Ion-Pair Induced Electrostatic Gating at Buried Interface for Efficient, Stable, and Eco-Safe Perovskite Solar Cells.
summary: The commercialization of perovskite solar cells (PSCs) is severely limited by interfacial charge losses, poor stability, and lead leakage, with few strategies to address all issues simultaneously. We design 1,5-naphthalenedisulfonic acid sodium salt (NSA) as a multifunctional buried interface modifier for SnO2-based PSCs. NSA features sulfonate groups, a rigid π-conjugated naphthalene backbone, and localized SO3--Na+ ion pairs, enabling an ion-pair-induced electrostatic gating effect beyond conventional chemical passivation: (i) sulfonate groups coordinate with undercoordinated Pb2+ defects to reduce trap density; (ii) the SO3--Na+ network generates a local electrostatic field to promote directional electron extraction and suppress hole backflow; (iii) the uniform NSA layer guides perovskite crystallization, producing larger grains and higher crystallinity. As a result, NSA-modified n-i-p PSCs reach a champion efficiency of 25.82%, with improved charge extraction and suppressed nonradiative recombination. Notably, the NSA layer acts as a robust lead-lock barrier, reducing lead leakage and boosting operational stability. This work presents a facile molecular design for buried interface engineering that synergistically optimizes efficiency, stability, and environmental safety in PSCs.

title: Ion Transport through Permselective Nanochannels of 2D-Covalent Organic Frameworks: Insights from Nonequilibrium Atomistic MD Simulations.
summary: Covalent organic frameworks (COFs), with their long-range crystallinity, rigidity, and highly tunable molecular porosity, are evolving as promising next-generation ion-permselective membranes for ion separation, reverse electrodialysis, and osmotic energy conversion. Herein, we employ steady-state nonequilibrium molecular dynamics (SS-NEMD) simulations to accurately and realistically describe the concentration-driven ion permeation process through functionalized and charged COF membranes and gain a fundamental understanding of the factors governing the ion transport in COFs. To this end, we model the diffusion of K+ and Cl- ions through the COF membranes that are suspended in aqueous electrolyte and are decorated with either propanesulfonic acid or sulfonic acid-terminated oligo(n)-ethylene glycol chains. We systematically vary the percentage of charged groups present within the nanoporous domains and demonstrate that the ion permeation, and thus the ion selectivity in these systems, depends on the concentration gradient of ions across the membrane, as modulated by the presence and degree/percentage of charged groups within the COF membranes. We further demonstrate that COF membranes decorated with charged oligo(n)-ethylene glycol chains show enhanced ion selectivity ratios, even when partially charged, reaching efficiencies of around 99% when compared to COFs with alkylated chains that show efficiencies of around 80%.

screen.tldr: Nonequilibrium MD studies ion permeation and selectivity in functionalized 2D COF membranes, showing charged side chains strongly enhance K+/Cl- separation.
screen.transfer_note: Atomistic simulation workflows and pore-functionalization effects could inform transport modeling in porous crystalline materials relevant to MCSP-adjacent design.

AI.tldr: The paper uses steady-state nonequilibrium molecular dynamics to study ion transport through functionalized covalent organic framework (COF) membranes and shows that charged oligo(ethylene glycol)-decorated COFs achieve much higher ion selectivity than alkylated ones.
AI.motivation: COFs are promising ion-permselective membranes for ion separation and energy conversion, but the molecular factors controlling ion permeation and selectivity are not fully understood.
AI.method: The authors simulated K+ and Cl- diffusion through aqueous COF membranes using SS-NEMD, comparing membranes functionalized with propanesulfonic acid or sulfonic acid-terminated oligo(n)-ethylene glycol chains while systematically varying the fraction of charged groups in the pores.
AI.result: Ion permeation and selectivity were found to depend on the ion concentration gradient and the amount of charged groups in the COF. Membranes with charged oligo(ethylene glycol) chains showed selectivity efficiencies near 99%, whereas alkylated-chain COFs reached about 80%.
AI.conclusion: Charged functional groups, especially sulfonic acid-terminated oligo(ethylene glycol) chains, substantially improve COF membrane ion selectivity, indicating that charge density and pore functionalization are key design parameters for high-performance ion-separation membranes.

title: Elucidating CO2 dynamics in high-entropy MOF-74 via machine learning interatomic potentials.
summary: High entropy variants of MOF-74 have demonstrated enhanced CO2 adsorption performance, yet it remains unclear whether homogenous metal mixing alone produces intrinsic enhancements in transport beyond the behavior of single metal parents. We develop a transferable machine-learned interatomic potential and perform large-scale molecular dynamics simulations of CO2 diffusion in MOF-74 with M = Mg, Co, Cu, Ni, and Zn, together with mixed-metal frameworks including a near-equimolar high-entropy composition, an experimentally reported ratio, and M-rich 2 : 1 : 1 : 1 : 1 variants. At 300 K, single-metal axial diffusivities span 0.322 to 1.211 × 10-8 m2 s-1, with Mg slowest and Cu fastest. Strikingly, the near-equimolar high-entropy framework exhibits Dz = 0.899 × 10-8 m2 s-1, reproduced within a few percent by a composition-weighted rule-of-mixtures built from the single-metal parents, and the same rule holds for the experimentally reported ratio and for M-rich mixtures. Temperature-dependent simulations from 300 to 500 K follow Arrhenius behavior with activation energies of 0.044-0.099 eV and prefactors of 6-15 × 10-8 m2 s-1, while the high-entropy framework remains within the parent range across the full window. These results establish a clean-limit transport baseline for compositionally complex MOF-74 and identify a simple, predictive rule for CO2 diffusivity in homogeneous mixed-metal frameworks, providing a quantitative reference for assessing when experimentally relevant factors drive departures from rule-of-mixtures behavior.

screen.transfer_note: Transferable MLIPs and large-scale MD could accelerate screening of flexible porous crystals and mixed-metal frameworks relevant to adsorption and stability.

AI.tldr: The study uses machine-learned molecular dynamics to show that CO2 diffusion in mixed-metal MOF-74 is largely predictable from the single-metal parents via a simple rule of mixtures, with no intrinsic transport boost from high-entropy mixing alone.
AI.motivation: The authors wanted to determine whether homogeneous metal mixing in high-entropy MOF-74 creates transport advantages beyond those of the pure-metal frameworks, since enhanced CO2 adsorption had already been observed but diffusion effects were unclear.
AI.method: A transferable machine-learned interatomic potential was developed and used in large-scale molecular dynamics simulations of CO2 diffusion in MOF-74 with single metals (Mg, Co, Cu, Ni, Zn) and several mixed-metal compositions, including a near-equimolar high-entropy case, an experimentally reported ratio, and M-rich 2:1:1:1:1 variants. Diffusivities were computed at 300 K and over 300-500 K to extract Arrhenius parameters.
AI.result: At 300 K, axial diffusivities for single-metal MOF-74 ranged from 0.322 to 1.211 × 10^-8 m^2 s^-1, with Mg slowest and Cu fastest. The near-equimolar high-entropy framework had Dz = 0.899 × 10^-8 m^2 s^-1, closely matched by a composition-weighted rule of mixtures. The same agreement held for the experimentally reported and M-rich mixtures. Across 300-500 K, diffusion followed Arrhenius behavior with activation energies of 0.044-0.099 eV and prefactors of 6-15 × 10^-8 m^2 s^-1.
AI.conclusion: Homogeneous high-entropy mixing in MOF-74 does not by itself produce anomalous CO2 transport; instead, diffusivity is well described by a simple composition-weighted baseline. title: A Water-Stable Ultramicroporous Metal-Organic Framework with Aromatic Pore Walls for Coal-Mine Methane Capture.
summary: Selective separation of methane (CH4) from nitrogen-rich coal-mine methane remains challenging owing to their similar physicochemical properties. Here we report a water-stable ultramicroporous metal-organic framework, Ni(Hbzza)2, featuring densely packed aromatic pore walls that create a π-enriched confined environment for CH4 adsorption. The 3-fold interpenetrated architecture generates narrow channels that may strengthen London dispersion interactions with CH4, affording an uptake of 40 cm3 g-1 at 298 K and a CH4/N2 selectivity of 5.6 (IAST). Breakthrough experiments demonstrate efficient dynamic separation under both dilute and humid conditions.

screen.tldr: Water-stable ultramicroporous MOF with aromatic pore walls selectively adsorbs methane over nitrogen, aided by confined dispersion interactions and interpenetrated channels.
screen.transfer_note: MOF pore-environment design and adsorption selectivity modeling could inform crystal packing and host-guest interaction strategies in molecular crystals.

AI.tldr: A water-stable ultramicroporous metal-organic framework, Ni(Hbzza)2, was designed to selectively adsorb methane over nitrogen by using π-rich, tightly confined pores that enhance methane–framework interactions.
AI.motivation: Separating methane from nitrogen-rich coal-mine methane is difficult because CH4 and N2 have very similar physical properties, so improved adsorbents are needed for efficient purification.
AI.method: The authors synthesized a 3-fold interpenetrated Ni-based metal-organic framework with narrow channels and aromatic pore walls, then evaluated its CH4/N2 adsorption behavior using equilibrium uptake measurements, IAST selectivity analysis, and breakthrough experiments under dilute and humid conditions.
AI.result: Ni(Hbzza)2 showed a CH4 uptake of 40 cm3 g-1 at 298 K and a CH4/N2 selectivity of 5.6 by IAST, and it performed well in dynamic breakthrough tests even in the presence of moisture.
AI.conclusion: The study demonstrates that pore confinement combined with π-enriched aromatic environments can improve methane capture and separation from nitrogen, making Ni(Hbzza)2 a promising adsorbent for practical coal-mine methane upgrading.

title: Symmetry Engineering of Metal-Organic Frameworks via Ligand Desymmetrization Design for Acetylene Purification.
summary: High-purity acetylene (C2H2) is an important chemical feedstock, yet removing the unavoidable acidic impurity carbon dioxide (CO2) remains energy-intensive using conventional methods. Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), with tunable pore structures and abundant active sites, have attracted considerable attention for C2H2/CO2 separation. However, most reported MOFs struggle to simultaneously achieve high adsorption capacity and selectivity. In this work, ligand desymmetrization combined with a mixed-ligand strategy was employed to modulate framework symmetry, leading to the construction of two Cu-based MOFs (ZJNU-501 and ZJNU-502) with distinct pore architectures. ZJNU-501, with lower symmetry, preserves a higher density of open metal sites (OMSs) and more complex pore environments. As a result, it exhibits a C2H2 uptake of 118 cm3 g-1 at 298 K and a C2H2/CO2 selectivity of 3.2. Dynamic breakthrough experiments show that ZJNU-501 can produce C2H2 with a purity of 99.5% at a productivity of 1.33 mol kg-1 under ambient conditions, together with good cycling stability. In contrast, ZJNU-502 shows moderate performance due to its higher symmetry and reduced OMS density. This work not only confirms the potential of using the ligand desymmetrization strategy in constructing complex pore structures but also demonstrates the application of such materials in addressing energy-critical separation technologies.

screen.tldr: Ligand desymmetrization tunes MOF symmetry and open metal-site density, improving acetylene/carbon dioxide separation performance in two Cu-based frameworks.
screen.transfer_note: Symmetry-controlled ligand design and pore-environment engineering could inform how structural motifs affect adsorption and packing in crystalline materials.

AI.tldr: The paper reports two Cu-based MOFs designed via ligand desymmetrization and a mixed-ligand strategy for C2H2/CO2 separation. The lower-symmetry framework, ZJNU-501, retains more open metal sites and achieves better acetylene uptake, selectivity, and breakthrough performance than ZJNU-502.
AI.motivation: Separating trace CO2 from high-purity acetylene is important but energy-intensive with conventional methods. The study aims to create MOFs that combine high adsorption capacity with effective C2H2/CO2 selectivity by tuning framework symmetry and pore environment.
AI.method: The authors used ligand desymmetrization together with a mixed-ligand synthesis approach to build two Cu-based MOFs, ZJNU-501 and ZJNU-502, with different symmetries and pore architectures. They then evaluated gas adsorption, selectivity, and dynamic breakthrough behavior under ambient conditions.
AI.result: ZJNU-501, the lower-symmetry MOF, preserved a higher density of open metal sites and more complex pores, giving a C2H2 uptake of 118 cm3 g-1 at 298 K and a C2H2/CO2 selectivity of 3.2. In breakthrough tests, it produced 99.5% pure C2H2 with a productivity of 1.33 mol kg-1 and showed good cycling stability. ZJNU-502 performed less well due to higher symmetry and fewer open metal sites.
AI.conclusion: Ligand desymmetrization is an effective design strategy for creating MOFs with favorable pore complexity and active-site density. The work demonstrates that such structural tuning can improve practical C2H2/CO2 separation and support energy-efficient gas purification.

title: Regulating the Electronic Structure via Multi-Transition Metals in Nanoporous High-Entropy Perovskites for Boosted Alkaline Hydrogen Evolution.
summary: High-entropy perovskite oxides (HEPOs) exhibit great application prospects in electrocatalysis due to their enormous compositional design space. Herein, nanoporous La-based HEPOs were synthesized for the first time through a dealloying and annealing strategy, and employed as electrocatalysts for alkaline hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). The HEPOs exhibit single-phase cubic perovskite structures and three-dimensional nanoporous architecture. Among them, L5M-0Cr (La(Ni0.2Mn0.2Fe0.2Co0.2Ru0.2)O3-δ) demonstrates exceptional alkaline HER activity, achieving a low overpotential of ∼50.6 mV at -10 mA cm- 2 and a small Tafel slope of ∼60.1 mV dec- 1, surpassing most reported perovskite-based catalysts and exceeding Pt/C at high current densities. Additionally, L5M-0Cr shows remarkable stability over 120 h of continuous operation and delivers promising performance in overall water-splitting systems. Structural characterizations, in situ Raman spectroscopy, and density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that lattice distortion and charge redistribution within high-entropy systems can effectively modulate electronic structure, inducing strong hybridization between Ru 4d and O 2p orbitals. Theoretical simulations are employed to establish the volcano-type correlation between hydrogen adsorption free energy (ΔG*H) and HER exchange current density (log i0). This work demonstrates that high-entropy design synergistically optimizes the structural, electronic, and catalytic properties of perovskites, providing a promising strategy for developing efficient electrocatalysts in energy conversion applications.

AI.motivation: To address the need for efficient, durable, and low-cost electrocatalysts for alkaline hydrogen evolution, the authors explore the large compositional space of high-entropy perovskite oxides and aim to use structural and electronic disorder to improve catalytic performance.
AI.method: Nanoporous La-based HEPOs were synthesized by dealloying followed by annealing, then characterized by structural analysis, in situ Raman spectroscopy, and density functional theory calculations. Their electrocatalytic performance was evaluated for alkaline HER and overall water splitting, with correlations drawn between hydrogen adsorption energetics and exchange current density.
AI.result: The single-phase cubic nanoporous HEPOs showed strong HER activity, especially L5M-0Cr (La(Ni0.2Mn0.2Fe0.2Co0.2Ru0.2)O3-δ), which achieved an overpotential of about 50.6 mV at -10 mA cm-2, a Tafel slope of about 60.1 mV dec-1, and stable operation for over 120 h. It also performed well in overall water splitting. Experiments and theory indicated that lattice distortion and charge redistribution enhanced Ru 4d–O 2p hybridization and optimized hydrogen adsorption behavior.
AI.conclusion: High-entropy design is an effective strategy to tune the structure and electronic properties of perovskite oxides, enabling synergistic improvements in catalytic activity and stability. The work suggests nanoporous HEPOs are promising electrocatalysts for hydrogen production and broader energy conversion applications.

title: Lewis-Base Coordination Enables Highly Dispersed Pt Cocatalyst on Pyrene-Based MOFs for Enhanced Photocatalytic Hydrogen Evolution.
summary: Rationally optimizing the coordination structures of Pt-based cocatalysts to concurrently achieve enhanced charge separation/transfer and lowered reaction energy barriers is significant for photocatalysis. Herein, we engineered the coordination of Pt cocatalyst on pyrene-based metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) through grafting different Lewis-base groups. The softness of the introduced groups directly determines their affinity for Pt precursors, allowing for precise tailoring of the electronic metal-support interactions (EMSI) of Pt and MOFs, which leads to the distinct Pt coordination structures. These structural features accelerate charge separation/transfer by an established internal electric field and lower catalytic energy barriers enabled by the oxidized Pt surface, leading to significantly enhanced photocatalytic activity. Specifically, the -SH-functionalized MOF (Pt/NU-M), featuring strong EMSI, achieves atomic dispersion of Pt-O/S coordination and delivers a superior hydrogen evolution rate of 5.68 mmol gcat -1 h-1 (405.71 mmol gpt -1 h-1) when using ascorbic acid as a sacrificial agent upon full-spectrum light irradiation, which is about 16 times higher than that of the Pt/NU control and surpasses many reported MOF-based materials. Notably, the catalyst maintains exceptional stability over 20 h of continuous operation. This work highlights Lewis-base coordination for tailoring active sites and optimizing EMSI, providing new insights for rational catalyst design and related energy applications.

screen.tldr: Lewis-base functionalization tunes Pt coordination on pyrene-based MOFs, improving electronic metal-support interactions and photocatalytic hydrogen evolution performance.

AI.tldr: The paper reports a coordination-engineering strategy to tune Pt cocatalyst structures on pyrene-based MOFs, improving charge separation and lowering reaction barriers for photocatalytic hydrogen evolution.
AI.motivation: The goal is to rationally optimize Pt-based cocatalysts so they can simultaneously promote efficient charge transfer and reduce catalytic energy barriers, which are both critical for high-performance photocatalysis.
AI.method: Different Lewis-base groups were grafted onto a pyrene-based MOF to control Pt precursor affinity and thereby tune electronic metal-support interactions (EMSI). This produced distinct Pt coordination environments, including atomic Pt-O/S coordination in the -SH-functionalized MOF (Pt/NU-M).
AI.result: Pt/NU-M showed strong EMSI, an internal electric-field-assisted charge separation/transfer process, and an oxidized Pt surface that lowered reaction barriers. It achieved a hydrogen evolution rate of 5.68 mmol gcat−1 h−1 (405.71 mmol gpt−1 h−1) under full-spectrum irradiation with ascorbic acid, about 16 times higher than the Pt/NU control, and remained stable for 20 h.
AI.conclusion: Lewis-base coordination is an effective way to tailor Pt active-site structure and EMSI in MOF photocatalysts, offering a practical design principle for improving photocatalytic energy conversion systems.

title: Phase-Dependent Functionality and Defect-Induced Magnetism in Monolayer SnTe Polymorphs.
summary: Monolayer SnTe offers an unusual opportunity for functional materials design because its electronic and magnetic behavior can be tuned through two coupled control parameters: crystal phase and local defect chemistry. Here, first-principles calculations establish how these complementary design knobs govern the intrinsic and defect-driven properties of four SnTe polymorphs. Among the considered monolayers, cubic SnTe is identified as the ground-state phase, closely followed by γ-SnTe, while hexagonal and β'-SnTe are less favorable. This phase hierarchy is accompanied by strongly distinct electronic and transport regimes, with the HSE+SOC band gap spanning 0.35-1.84 eV, ultrahigh hole mobility emerging in cubic SnTe, strongly anisotropic electron transport appearing in hexagonal SnTe, and anisotropic hole transport found in β'-SnTe. Guided by this phase-stability landscape, defect engineering is then examined in cubic and γ-SnTe through substitutional doping and native vacancies. A clear phase-dependent defect response is revealed: dopants drive cubic SnTe toward effective metallicity, whereas γ-SnTe supports more selective outcomes, ranging from metallic to semiconducting behavior depending on dopant species. In particular, Mn is the most favorable magnetic dopant in both phases, and Mn-doped γ-SnTe combines strong spin polarization with a retained direct band gap, highlighting it as a promising magnetic semiconducting state. Together, these results show that phase selection defines the intrinsic band gap and transport landscape of monolayer SnTe, while defect engineering provides additional control over metallicity, magnetism, and carrier polarity. Monolayer SnTe therefore emerges as a tunable platform for infrared optoelectronic and spin-functional applications.

screen.tldr: First-principles study of monolayer SnTe polymorphs shows phase-dependent stability, transport, and defect-driven magnetism, with Mn-doped γ-SnTe emerging as a magnetic semiconductor.

AI.tldr: The paper uses first-principles calculations to show that monolayer SnTe can be tuned by choosing its crystal phase and introducing defects. Cubic SnTe is the most stable phase, γ-SnTe is close behind, and the phases differ strongly in band gap and carrier transport. Defect engineering, especially Mn doping, can induce metallicity and magnetism, with Mn-doped γ-SnTe standing out as a spin-polarized semiconductor.
AI.motivation: To identify how crystal phase and defect chemistry jointly control the electronic, transport, and magnetic properties of monolayer SnTe, enabling rational design for optoelectronic and spin-functional devices.
AI.method: First-principles calculations were performed on four SnTe polymorphs to compare phase stability, electronic structure, and carrier transport. Hybrid functional calculations with spin-orbit coupling were used for band gaps and related properties. Defect studies focused on substitutional dopants and native vacancies in cubic and γ-SnTe to assess metallicity, magnetism, and carrier behavior.
AI.result: Cubic SnTe is the ground-state phase, with γ-SnTe slightly less stable; hexagonal and β'-SnTe are less favorable. The HSE+SOC band gap ranges from 0.35 to 1.84 eV across phases. Cubic SnTe shows ultrahigh hole mobility, hexagonal SnTe shows strongly anisotropic electron transport, and β'-SnTe shows anisotropic hole transport. Defects have phase-dependent effects: dopants tend to make cubic SnTe effectively metallic, while γ-SnTe can become metallic or remain semiconducting depending on the dopant. Mn is the best magnetic dopant in both phases, and Mn-doped γ-SnTe preserves a direct band gap while exhibiting strong spin polarization.
AI.conclusion: Crystal phase selection sets the intrinsic electronic and transport baseline of monolayer SnTe, while defect engineering provides additional control over conductivity, magnetism, and carrier type. This makes monolayer SnTe a promising platform for infrared optoelectronics and spintronic applications.

title: Porous Ni-based metal-organic frameworks reduce the oxygen evolution temperature of lithium perchlorate.
summary: The temperature at which inorganic oxidizers evolve oxygen is a key operational constraint in applications ranging from energetic materials to chemical oxygen generators and life-support systems. However, commonly used chlorates and perchlorates typically decompose at temperatures exceeding 400 °C, imposing limitations on efficiency, thermal management, and materials compatibility and motivating strategies for lower-temperature oxygen release without sacrificing yield. Here, porous Ni-based metal-organic frameworks catalyze LiClO4 decomposition, lowering oxygen evolution onset temperatures by up to 180 °C relative to pure LiClO4 while preserving >95 mol% O2 yield. Framework porosity enables oxidizer melt-infiltration and promotes intimate nanoscale oxidizer-catalyst contact, enhancing catalytic effectiveness relative to the most effective nonporous Ni catalyst identified through Ni-salt screening. This approach demonstrates how framework porosity can be leveraged to enhance oxidizer-catalyst interactions and improve catalytic efficiency in oxygen-generating systems through structural design rather than solely through metal identity or loading, enabling lower-temperature oxygen release without compromising oxygen yield.

screen.tldr: Porous Ni-based MOFs catalyze lithium perchlorate decomposition, lowering oxygen-release temperature by improving oxidizer-catalyst contact while preserving high oxygen yield.

AI.tldr: Porous Ni-based metal-organic frameworks significantly lower the oxygen-release temperature of LiClO4 decomposition by up to 180 °C while maintaining over 95 mol% O2 yield, mainly by enabling better oxidizer-catalyst contact through porosity.
AI.motivation: Conventional chlorates and perchlorates decompose above 400 °C, which creates problems for efficiency, thermal management, and materials compatibility in oxygen-generating and energetic applications. The work seeks a lower-temperature oxygen-release strategy without reducing oxygen yield.
AI.method: The study uses porous Ni-based metal-organic frameworks as catalysts for LiClO4 decomposition and compares their performance with pure LiClO4 and with nonporous Ni catalysts identified through Ni-salt screening. The key design feature is framework porosity, which allows oxidizer melt-infiltration and nanoscale catalyst-oxidizer contact.
AI.result: The porous Ni-MOF catalysts reduce the oxygen evolution onset temperature by up to 180 °C relative to pure LiClO4 while preserving greater than 95 mol% O2 yield. They outperform the most effective nonporous Ni catalyst from the screening study.
AI.conclusion: Structural design, especially porosity, can be more important than metal identity alone for improving oxidizer-catalyst interactions. Porous Ni-based frameworks offer an effective route to lower-temperature oxygen release without sacrificing oxygen yield.

title: High-Performance Solid Composite Electrolyte with Bifunctional Metal-Organic Frameworks as Active Fillers for All-Solid-State Lithium Batteries.
summary: In this work, a solid composite electrolyte (SCE) was prepared by incorporating a lithiated bifunctional metal-organic framework (UiO-66-SO3Li-NH2-0.85) into a PVDF-HFP/LiTFSI polymer matrix. Specifically, the lithiated sulfonate groups provide uniformly distributed lithium-ion conduction sites, while the amino groups achieve good interfacial bonding in the composite. Consequently, the optimized SCE delivers a high ionic conductivity of 5.01 × 10-4 S cm-1 (60 °C), its lithium-ion transference number is measured to be 0.65, and it possesses a wide electrochemical stability window (4.9 V). Furthermore, the assembled all-solid-state Li∥SCE∥LFP full cells also demonstrates a reversible capacity of 147.45 mAh g-1 after 120 cycles at 0.2C (60 °C) and a capacity of 113 mAh g-1 at 1C after 60 cycles (25 °C). This bifunctional MOF strategy has made it the subject of intense research for high-performance all-solid-state lithium batteries.

screen.tldr: Bifunctional UiO-66-based MOF fillers improve polymer solid electrolyte conductivity, lithium transference, and battery cycling in all-solid-state lithium cells.

title: Kinetically controlled crystallization via plant-derived additives boosts the efficiency of carbon-based perovskite solar cells exceeding 20%
summary: Effectively controlling crystallization kinetics to obtain high-quality perovskite films with large grains and low defect density is a key strategy for fabricating high-performance hole transport layer-free carbon-based perovskite solar cells (C-PSCs). Herein, a natural plant-derived molecule, locust bean gum (LBG), was introduced into the precursor solution to regulate the crystallization process of perovskites. The addition of LBG more effectively promotes the transformation of PbI2 into PbI3− complexes as prenucleation clusters to accelerate the nucleation process. Meanwhile, the growth rate of perovskite grains during annealing is significantly slowed down due to the stronger interaction between the precursor material and LBG. Benefiting from such rapid nucleation and slow crystallization, high-quality perovskite films with larger crystal sizes and optimized energy level arrangements have been formed. Consequently, the optimized C-PSC achieved a maximum power conversion efficiency of 20.23%, surpassing the efficiency of 18.22% for control devices. Additionally, the long-term stability testing demonstrates excellent storage stability and enhanced light stability under illumination. These findings provide new insights into the potential of natural plant-derived additives for achieving higher-performance perovskite photovoltaic devices.

title: Neodymium-based B-site high-entropy perovskite oxide nanoparticles as an efficient electrocatalyst for water splitting and methanol oxidation.
summary: High-entropy perovskite oxides are promising multifunctional electrocatalysts due to their complex defect structures derived from multi-elemental compositions. In this work, a Nd-based high-entropy perovskite, Nd(CoNiFeMn)O3-δ (NCNFM), was synthesized using a sol-gel route to investigate the effect of B-site configurational disorder on oxygen non-stoichiometry and electrocatalytic behaviour. Structural characterization reveals the formation of a single-phase perovskite with randomly distributed transition-metal cations at the B-site. The NCNFM catalyst was deposited on nickel foam and evaluated for the oxygen and hydrogen evolution reactions (OER and HER), overall water splitting (OWS), and the methanol oxidation reaction (MOR). NCNFM demonstrated outstanding bifunctional activity, achieving overpotentials of 350 mV for the OER and 144 mV for the HER at 10 mA cm-2, with Tafel slopes of 91.2 and 105 mV dec-1, respectively, outperforming the other perovskite oxides. It obtained a cell voltage of 1.67 V at 10 mA cm-2 and maintained stability for 72 hours in a self-supported two-electrode OWS system. NCNFM also showed superior MOR activity with a low onset potential of 1.467 V vs. RHE@100 mA cm-2, a low Tafel slope of 49 mV dec-1, and superior stability for at least 72 hours. The excellent catalytic behaviour of NCNFM is attributed to the synergistic effects among multiple B-site cations and the influence of configurational entropy, which enhance oxygen vacancy concentration and overall electrocatalytic activity.

title: Thermally Robust Broadband NIR‐II Emission Enabled by Dual‐Site Ni 2+ Occupancy in Double Perovskite
summary: Broadband and thermally robust near‐infrared (NIR) emitters are essential for advanced photonic applications from night‐vision imaging to biological sensing and spectroscopy. However, transition‐metal‐activated phosphors face an intrinsic coupling between emission bandwidth and thermal stability, with ultrabroad spectra accompanied by severe thermal quenching. Here, we demonstrate a dual‐site occupancy strategy mitigating this trade‐off by enabling Ni 2+ to occupy two crystallographically distinct octahedral sites in double perovskite Ca 2 AlTaO 6 . The optimized Ca 2 AlTaO 6 :Ni 2+ phosphor exhibits broadband NIR‐II emission (1050–1650 nm) with a 225 nm full width at half maximum, retaining 61% of room‐temperature luminescence intensity at 423 K. Spectral deconvolution, lifetime analysis, and structural characterization reveal the concentration‐dependent emission peak red‐shift (1260 → 1310 nm) originates from dynamic Ni 2+ redistribution between the two sites, with controllable spectral broadening. This site‐selective emission mechanism provides a reliable route for tunable NIR‐II spectral engineering. A phosphor‐converted LED based on a commercial red excitation chip delivers efficient NIR‐II output, validated in night‐vision imaging, biological tissue transillumination, and qualitative chemical identification. These results establish dual‐site occupancy as a viable, generalizable design principle for broadband, thermally stable NIR emitters, with direct relevance to photonic light‐source engineering.

title: Donor-Acceptor-Donor Type Diimidazole-Based Metal-Organic Framework for Photocatalytic C-O and C-C Bond Formation.
summary: The development of robust, efficient, and recyclable heterogeneous photocatalysts for solar-driven organic synthesis remains a significant challenge. Under visible-light irradiation, JNU-228 efficiently catalyzes the hydroxylation of arylboronic acids and the trifluoromethylation of coumarins and indoles. Moreover, JNU-228 maintains its structural integrity and catalytic activity over multiple cycles. This work demonstrates that incorporating molecular D-A-D photosensitizers into stable MOF matrices is a powerful strategy for developing superior heterogeneous photocatalysts for sustainable organic transformations.

title: The structural stability and temperature-dependent exciton dynamics of CsPbBr3 millimeter crystals.
summary: Understanding the intrinsic lattice properties and exciton dynamics of halide perovskites is crucial for the rational optimization of their optoelectronic performance. Here, density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that CsPbBr3 exhibits no imaginary phonon modes, confirming its dynamical stability. The calculated Pugh's ratio (2.47) and Poisson's ratio (0.32) indicate pronounced ductility, suggesting a soft lattice favorable for electron-phonon coupling. To experimentally probe the intrinsic optical response free from surface and size effects, CsPbBr3 millimeter crystals were successfully synthesized via an anti-solvent vapor-assisted crystallization method. Under single-photon excitation, dual emission peaks at 525 and 555 nm are observed, attributed to free exciton (FE) and bound exciton (BE) recombination, respectively. Under two-photon excitation, only BE emission remains due to reabsorption of higher-energy FE emission. As the temperature increases, the photoluminescence intensity decreases and the emission spectrum broadens due to enhanced nonradiative recombination. Under femtosecond excitation, the lifetime is 1.61 ns, indicating carrier-induced activation of bulk defects. These results elucidate the exciton recombination dynamics and electron-phonon interaction mechanisms in bulk CsPbBr3, highlighting its potential for optoelectronic and photovoltaic applications based on fully inorganic halide perovskites.

title: Utilization of Robust Zr-Based Metal–Organic Framework for Efficient N2/H2 Separation
summary: The development of energy-efficient separation technologies for nitrogen (N2)–hydrogen (H2) mixtures under conventional industrial conditions remains a critical challenge. Adsorptive separation emerges as a promising strategy, contingent upon the design of high-performance adsorbents with tailored physicochemical properties. By integrating static adsorption isotherms, dynamic breakthrough experiments, and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, we comprehensively characterize the adsorption mechanisms and diffusion kinetics. The results demonstrate that UiO-66-F4 exhibits optimal performance in capturing N2 from N2-H2 mixtures under simulated industrial conditions, owing to its balanced binding affinity, high nitrogen uptake, and favorable micro-/mesoporous diffusion dynamics. This work offers a promising alternative for N2-H2 separation in industrial applications.

title: Smart Hydrogen-Bonded Organic Frameworks: From Design Rules to Applications.
summary: Crystalline porous materials have evolved significantly with the advent of metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) and covalent organic frameworks (COFs), yet hydrogen-bonded organic frameworks (HOFs) represent a distinct paradigm shift from static to adaptive porosity. Unlike their coordination- or covalent-bonded counterparts, HOFs are assembled via weak, reversible hydrogen interactions, endowing the framework with intrinsic "softness" and adaptive flexibility. This unique structural nature allows for reversible transformations─such as breathing, gate-opening, and layer sliding─in response to external stimuli. In this perspective, we systematically discuss the design rules of smart HOFs, highlighting how specific flexibility mechanisms are translated into advanced functionalities across four pivotal domains. We explore how adaptive pore environments enable the discrimination of similar-sized molecules and "self-healing" capabilities in separation processes, and how structural perturbations are converted into readable optical or electrical signals for precise sensing. Furthermore, we examine the leveraging of dynamic luminescence and topological switching for smart optoelectronics and information security, as well as the utilization of stimuli-responsive drug release and biocompatibility for precision biomedical therapy. Finally, we provide a critical outlook on the future challenges regarding stability, predictability, and processability, aiming to bridge the gap between theoretical design and practical deployment of smart HOF materials.

AI.conclusion: Smart HOFs offer a promising route to responsive porous materials, but major challenges remain in stability, predictability, and processability before they can be broadly deployed in real-world applications.

title: Efficient dual adsorption of toxic anionic dyes Congo Red and Rose Bengal from wastewater by 2D Cd-MOF.
summary: The contamination from industrial dyes has caused serious environmental and health-related consequences. Different materials have been used as adsorbents to solve this issue but conventional adsorbents suffer from challenges like their ability to be reused and their insufficient adsorption capacity. The immediate need exists for creating new efficient adsorbent materials that can remove the dyes while protecting the environment. The emerging family of Metal-Organic Frameworks (MOFs) demonstrates crystalline structures and exceptional properties enabling outstanding adsorption applications in wastewater treatment. In this work, a solvothermal method was used to synthesize cadmium-based metal-organic framework (Cd-MOF) which exhibited remarkable efficiency in removing Congo Red (CR) (500 mg/g) and Rose Bengal (RB) (99.44 mg/g) dyes. Adsorption properties of Cd-MOF function reliably over a pH range of 5-9 which enables practical real-world application. Recycling performance confirmed that Cd-MOF maintained high adsorption efficiency throughout five cycles for CR (98.7%) and RB (86.6%), hence highlighting its potential to be reused in dye removal applications. The Cd-MOF exhibits high adsorption capacity and good reusability, demonstrating its potential as an efficient adsorbent for removing hazardous dyes from aqueous systems. These findings highlight the potential applications of MOFs for advanced wastewater treatment and encourage further development of greener, environmentally sustainable MOF technologies.

title: Halide-dependent photoelectrical response and charge transport in EVA-embedded Cs2TiClxBr6−x perovskite thin films
summary: Lead-free titanium halide perovskites with the formula Cs2TiClxBr6−x were integrated into an ethylene–vinyl acetate (EVA) matrix to form hybrid perovskite thin films with tunable optoelectronic properties. Importantly, this work goes beyond compositional tuning by demonstrating that the polymer–perovskite hybrid architecture actively governs interfacial charge transport and polarization phenomena. Structural and optical characterization confirmed the formation of vacancy-ordered double perovskites with visible-light absorption and photoluminescence features associated with defect-mediated electronic relaxation. The electrical and photoinduced responses of the composites were investigated using electrochemical impedance spectroscopy with symmetric fluorine-doped tin oxide (FTO)│EVA│FTO configurations. Upon illumination, the films exhibited a marked decrease in impedance, revealing the halide-dependent modulation of charge transport, interfacial polarization, and pseudocapacitive behavior. Mixed-halide compositions displayed improved electrical uniformity and reduced transport resistance compared to pristine EVA, indicating enhanced photoinduced charge dynamics. Hirshfeld surface analysis was employed as a structural descriptor to quantify halide surface exposure, thereby linking composition-dependent electronic localization to the observed photoelectrical response. As a functional demonstration of these charge dynamics, the hybrid films were also evaluated under photocatalytic conditions, where light-driven formate and hydrogen generation corroborated the effective charge separation inferred from impedance measurements.

title: From metal nodes to sulfur capture: design principles and challenges in MOF-based adsorptive desulfurization.
summary: The persistent presence of thiophenic sulfur compounds in fuels is a major challenge for achieving ultra-deep desulfurization because conventional methods struggle to remove stable aromatic molecules like DBT, BT, and 4,6-DMDBT. Their strong molecular rigidity, low reactivity, and steric hindrance limit the effectiveness of existing technologies, underscoring the urgent need for advanced materials capable of selectively capturing these recalcitrant sulfur species. Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) have emerged as promising materials for deep desulfurization, but selectively removing thiophenic sulfur compounds is still difficult because these molecules are highly stable and interact weakly with conventional adsorbents. This review tackles this issue by examining MOFs designed with π-rich linkers, mixed-valent metal centers, and unsaturated metal sites that improve sulfur capture through stronger π-π interactions, π-complexation, and metal-sulfur coordination. Unlike general surveys, this work uniquely integrates mechanistic insights, structure-property correlations, computational analysis, and real-fuel performance to establish clear design principles for high-efficiency adsorption. By critically comparing top-performing frameworks and highlighting advances in post-synthetic modification and composite development, the review outlines how rational structural tuning can overcome the limitations of traditional adsorbents. This unified perspective offers a strategic roadmap for guiding future research toward sustainable, high-performance MOF-based desulfurization technologies.

AI.method: The paper reviews MOFs featuring π-rich linkers, mixed-valent metal centers, and unsaturated metal sites, and compares their sulfur-capture mechanisms, including π-π interactions, π-complexation, and metal-sulfur coordination. It also integrates structure-property relationships, computational studies, real-fuel testing, post-synthetic modification, and composite design.
AI.result: The review identifies that rational structural tuning of MOFs can significantly improve selective adsorption of thiophenic sulfur compounds. It highlights top-performing frameworks and shows that mechanistic design principles can overcome limitations of traditional adsorbents.
AI.conclusion: MOFs are promising platforms for sustainable deep desulfurization, and future progress will depend on targeted material design that strengthens specific host-guest interactions while maintaining practical performance in real fuels.
